questionText:
Read the following case study on Mutation Breeding and Induced Polyploidy in Crop Improvement, and answer the questions that follow:

Mutation breeding has served as a powerful tool to generate novel genetic variability in self-pollinated field crops where natural germplasm reserves are exhausted. Induced mutagenesis exposes seeds or vegetative propagules to physical mutagens (ionizing radiations such as Gamma rays from Cobalt-60, X-rays, fast neutrons) or chemical mutagens (alkylating agents like Ethyl Methane Sulfonate / EMS, Sodium Azide). A celebrated milestone of mutation breeding in India was the evolution of the amber-grained wheat cultivar 'Sharbati Sonora' by Dr. M. S. Swaminathan and colleagues at IARI, New Delhi, by irradiating the red-grained Mexican dwarf wheat variety Sonora 64 with gamma rays. Beyond point mutations, manipulating ploidy levels (Polyploidy Breeding) has created revolutionary crop architectures. Autopolyploids are induced by treating dividing apical meristems with the plant alkaloid 'Colchicine' (extracted from autumn crocus Colchicum autumnale). Colchicine inhibits microtubule spindle fiber polymerization during mitotic metaphase, preventing chromatid separation and effectively doubling the chromosome number. In watermelon (Citrullus lanatus), crossing an induced autotetraploid (4n = 44) female with a normal diploid (2n = 22) male produces commercial triploid (3n = 33) hybrid seeds. Because triploid plants suffer severe meiotic chromosome unbalance during gametogenesis, they fail to form functional seeds, producing prize 'Seedless Watermelons'.

Question: Which of the following chemical mutagens is an alkylating agent widely used in plant mutation breeding to induce high-frequency transition mutations?

options.text: Sodium Chloride
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

For Popular Chemical Mutagen in Crop Plants (Agrometeorology, Genetics & Plant Breeding):
Ethyl Methane Sulfonate (EMS) is the most potent and widely deployed chemical mutagen, alkylating guanine to induce G:C to A:T transitions.

questionText:
Arrange the numerical ploidy levels in order of increasing total chromosome count for an organism with basic genome x = 7:
(A) Monosomic (2n - 1 = 13)
(B) Diploid (2n = 14)
(C) Triploid (3n = 21)
(D) Tetraploid (4n = 28)

Choose the correct chronological/logical sequence from the options given below:

options.text: A, C, B, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A, B, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text: B, A, C, D
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: D, B, C, A
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For x = 7: Monosomic has 13 (2n-1), Diploid has 14 (2n), Triploid has 21 (3n), and Tetraploid has 28 (4n).
Hence Option C is correct.
Hence, option (B) is correct.

questionText:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells maintaining the somatic chromosome number.
Statement II: Meiosis produces four genetically diverse haploid daughter gametes through two successive nuclear divisions.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is true while Statement II contains an error.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement I.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct: mitosis preserves the diploid somatic chromosome complement, whereas meiosis reduces it to the haploid gametic state.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (C) is correct.

topic: Fruit Crops and Standard Commercial Vegetative Propagation Methods
questionText:
Match the fruit crop in List I with its primary commercial vegetative propagation technique in List II:

List I:
(A) Mango (North India standard)
(B) Guava and Litchi
(C) Rose and Citrus
(D) Apple clonal rootstocks

List II:
(I) Side Veneer Grafting / Softwood Grafting
(II) Air Layering (Gootee / Marcottage) using sphagnum moss and IBA
(III) T-Budding (Shield Budding)
(IV) Stooling (Mound Layering)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Mango uses veneer/softwood grafting; Guava/Litchi use air layering; Rose/Citrus use T-budding; Apple clonal rootstocks are multiplied by stooling.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.
